t: The Spanish moved Havana to its present harbour in 1519, and from 1561 the ships bound for Spain were required to gather in its bay, which made it the main port of Spain’s American colonies.
Pirate attacks, beginning with the burning of 1555, led the Crown to fortify the city, and after the British siege of 1762 the Spanish made it the most heavily fortified city in the Americas.

Sugar and the slave trade brought riches to the city, slavery stayed legal in Cuba until 1886, and Havana became the capital of the independent Republic of Cuba in 1902 and the seat of the revolutionary government after 1959.
dyk: In 1763 Britain gave Havana back to Spain in return for Florida, less than a year after taking the city, and more than half of the British force that took it died, mostly of illness and in particular yellow fever.
ev: The town that became Havana is settled beside Puerto de Carenas, on the north coast
The French corsair Jacques de Sores takes Havana and burns much of it
A royal decree requires all ships bound for Spain to assemble in Havana Bay
Philip II of Spain grants Havana the title of city
A British fleet and army besiege and take Havana, which Spain recovers in 1763
The first railway in Cuba opens between Havana and Bejucal
Spain relinquishes sovereignty over Cuba after the sinking of the USS Maine in Havana harbour
The Cuban Revolution brings Fidel Castro’s government to power in Havana

f.founded: Diego Velázquez de Cuéllar founded San Cristóbal de la Habana in 1514 on the south coast of Cuba; that settlement failed, and the town that became Havana grew at its present site beside Puerto de Carenas in 1519.
f.where: On the northern coast of Cuba along the Straits of Florida, around a bay entered through a narrow inlet, with the Almendares River crossing the city from south to north.
f.known: A harbour on the Gulf Stream; the assembly point of the Spanish treasure fleet; forts and walls; the shipyard of El Arsenal; the British siege of 1762; the slave trade and sugar; the capital of the Republic of Cuba from 1902; the revolution of 1959
f.today: Havana is the capital and largest city of Cuba and is both a city and a province, with Old Havana on UNESCO’s World Heritage list.
